title: Synthetic probe suite and canary gating for embedding + reranker stability
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create an automated synthetic probe suite and CI + canary gating flow to detect embedding and reranker quality regressions tied to model/config changes. The goal is to provide fast, reproducible offline checks (recall/precision, nDCG), distributional drift signals, and automated canary decisions before and after deploys so platform and product teams can safely roll model/config updates with measurable guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Probe suite runs headless in CI within 20m for full probe set and <5m for a small smoke set
Defines baseline metrics and thresholds for recall@1/5/10, precision@k, nDCG, and mean cosine shift with annotated acceptable deltas
Automated canary gate: PRs that change model or reranker config must pass smoke probes to merge; staging rollout requires full probe pass before canary release
Alerts trigger when drift signal exceeds threshold or when core metrics drop beyond configured bounds; alert includes sample queries and top-k deltas
Dashboard with daily probe runs, historical trend, and per-config/model lineage available in Console
Rollback automation documented: fallback model/config and runbook with steps and run command references
metrics: Primary offline: recall@1, recall@5, recall@10 (target no more than 2% relative drop vs baseline for canary)
Precision@k and nDCG@10 (monitor absolute drops >0.03 for high-impact datasets)
Distributional: mean cosine similarity shift of top-1 embeddings (alert if drop >0.04), Wasserstein distance over pairwise cosine histogram
Drift window: 24h rolling and 7d aggregation with z-score normalization
Operational: CI runtime, flakiness rate (probe failures marked flaky if >1% of runs)
plan_steps: Design probe corpus: 3 slices - production anchors (sampled high-traffic queries), long-tail stressors, adversarial/paraphrase set
Implement probe generator tools: paraphrase via back-translation, typos/noise injector, length/subquery permutations
Create evaluation harness using existing eval infra: runner that calculates recall/precision/nDCG and embedding distribution stats
Add small smoke set (50 queries) for fast PR checks and larger nightly suite (~2k queries) for staging/regression windows
Define canonical baselines per model+config (stored as artifact with version tag) and migration logic for model family updates
Integrate into CI: pre-merge smoke run for PRs that touch embeddings/config; block merge on fail
Integrate canary flows: staging rollout executes full suite; if metrics degrade beyond threshold, abort canary and trigger rollback automation
Expose results to Console: time-series, per-probe diff, and top-k shift visualizations; add links to offending PR/commit
Create alerting rules in PagerDuty and Slack channel with sample hits and suggested mitigation steps
Write runbook and handoff to SRE and platforms for on-call guidance
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with PM (Priya Singh), Design (Aisha Kapoor), and SRE. Agreed on three probe slices and initial thresholds for recall and cosine shift.
2026-03-04: Prototype probe generator committed (GH: redwood-inference/probes#142). Smoke set generator producing stable paraphrases with deterministic seeds.
2026-03-06: Initial CI job created: ci/probes-smoke.yml — runs smoke suite on PRs touching ./models or ./configs. Observed median runtime ~3m 45s in linux-ci.

2026-03-09: First full harness run against staging models completed (artifact stored: s3://redwood-evals/ENG-22011/baseline-2026-03-09.json). Recorded drop on one long-tail slice; opened follow-up ENG-22045 to investigate reranker weighting.
2026-03-12: Canary gating proposal reviewed by Security & Compliance — no additional data retention concerns; KMS usage for baseline artifact signing approved.
Next: wire results into Console dashboards and add PagerDuty routing for high-impact alerts (owner: Liam Chen).
owner_notes: We should prioritize low-latency smoke runs to avoid blocking fast-moving PRs; heavier nightly runs can be scheduled off-peak. Consider sampling stratified by customer tier for better sensitivity to high-revenue customers. Track flakiness and add deterministic seeds to generators to reduce noise.
